changes: TFSDispatch restores the eighteen-entry word-offset table. It queues invalid selectors before returning paramErr. The released table retains all eighteen handler names and comments but later grew to 112 long offsets. FSControl returns the ROM version string 1.2A.

FSQueue, FSQueueSync, SyncWait, FSAsync, FSDispatch, and CmdDone retain the original queueing, asynchronous dispatch, search-path retry, and completion behavior. The ROM forwards only ExtFSErr to external file systems; the later NoMacDskErr case and error-code rewrite are absent.

The ROM queue-clearing entry FInitQueue is at $402A6C. The captured Ghidra symbols call it InitQueue and assign FInitQueue to the preceding cd_DispNext at $402A5A. The reconstruction follows the released routine bodies and records that naming difference.

DSHook retains the November 1985 mount retry, disk ejection, and command-period abort behavior. It restores the screen-saving path removed in 1992, using a 285-by-72 bitmap with 36-byte rows, a classic GrafPort, and two kilobytes of stack slop. It restores saved pixels when possible and otherwise requests a window update.

The disk-switch keyboard path compares the event character directly with one and two. It predates the ASCII conversion in the June 1989 history, so the documented keyboard-eject bug remains. The later third-drive support, manual-eject paths, allocation flags, and cache-flush call are omitted.

DoEject retains the eject notification callback, disk ejection, and error beep. Original file attribution, applicable 1984–1986 history, routine contracts, and matching instruction comments remain. Explicit branch sizes and PC-relative operands preserve the target encodings.

The FSCallAsync equate comment now describes the asynchronous-call flag. Its released declaration incorrectly labels the occupied byte as free. The restored FSVrsn, bitmap offsets, GrafPort size, and Macintosh Plus interrupt mask are recorded below.
historical_limits: The byte comparison verifies the emitted code and data. It does not recover lost source spelling or test disk-switch behavior on hardware.
